subject: RFI: Dedicated reservation planning and GPU fitment for AuroraTech inference
messages:

Cc: procurement@auroratech.com
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: RFI: Dedicated reservation sizing for AuroraTech inference

Hi Jasmine,

We're starting an RFI for long‑running inference of our generative search and reranking services. High level: 24/7 traffic across two US regions, peak 8k concurrent prompts/minute across short chat (avg 80 tokens) and longer summarization flows (avg 900 tokens). Our procurement team asked us to gather recommended committed capacity profiles (GPU families, counts, burst allowances) and expected P95 latency at steady state.

Can Redwood provide a reservation sizing worksheet and an initial fitment recommendation for A100/H100/L4 class GPUs? We can share usage CSVs if that helps — attaching a small sample.

Thanks,
Alex Morales
Infrastructure Lead, Aurora Tech

Alex — thanks for the sample and context. I've reviewed the CSV and sketched an initial approach. A few clarifying questions before we size: 

- Are the 8k concurrent prompts/minute evenly distributed between the two regions or skewed to one primary region?
- What SLOs are you targeting for P95 generation latency for chat and for long summarization (in ms)?
- Any model family constraints (are you fixed to a single model or tolerant of quantized variants / sharded variants)?

I'll attach our lightweight reservation template so you can drop in a fuller historic sample if available. Once I have the SLOs and regional split, I'll run a GPU-fit pass with K/V cache assumptions and return recommended mixes and a burst policy.

Next steps: you send region split + SLOs + fuller CSV; I'll loop in Solutions (cc: Karthik) and ML Ops (cc: Rishi) to validate the kernel and packing assumptions.

Forwarding Alex's sample and Jasmine's note. Quick internal take before we finalize the recipient proposal:

On Thu, 10 Jun 2027 at 2:03 PM Aurora Tech <infra@auroratech.com> wrote:
> High level: 24/7 traffic across two US regions, peak 8k concurrent prompts/minute across short chat (avg 80 tokens) and longer summarization flows (avg 900 tokens).

Rishi — can you run a fast fitment run with these assumptions? My preliminary thought: a mixed tier works best — H100s for the long‑context summarization (better FP16 throughput on long sequences), A100s or H100x for heavy generation, and cost‑efficient L4s for small-chat and reranking at scale with quantized models. We should propose: 

- Baseline reserved commit: 6x H100 (or equivalent) + 20x L4 (or equivalent) per primary region, with cross‑region fallback.
- Burst pool: additional 10–15 L4 equivalents for spiky egress; auto‑burst to hosted spare capacity with fair‑share throttling.
- Expected steady‑state P95: chat ~120–180ms; long summarization (900 tokens) ~850–1,200ms depending on batching and KV cache hit rate.

Please attach a quick pdf with the fit numbers so I can include in the client response.

— Karthik
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com

Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 08:55:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: RFI: Dedicated reservation sizing for AuroraTech inference

Attaching a short fitment export and assumptions PDF. Notes: 

- Input assumptions: 8k concurrent prompts/minute -> translates to ~133 requests/sec. Splitting traffic 70/30 to primary/secondary gives ~93 req/s primary. With average token lengths the effective tokens/sec load is ~(93 * avg tokens).
- Kernel/packing: Long summarization (900 toks) benefits from larger batch windows; we assume a 40–60ms batching window for the H100 pool, and 10–20ms for L4 small-chat.
- KV cache: 40% prefix reuse for chat flows reduces token generation by ~20% across the fleet — important for reducing H100 counts.
- Recommendation (per primary region): 5x H100-profile nodes (for long context and mixed workloads), 18x L4-profile nodes for small chat and reranks. Reserve these as committed; configure a 25% burst buffer (elastic shared pool) with automatic fallback rules.
- Expected steady‑state P95 (with KV cache & batching): chat 110–150ms, summarization 700–1,000ms.

I'll include the exported numbers in the attached PDF. Forward to the client with the worksheet and we can iterate on token SLO tradeoffs.

[attachment: gpu-fit-analysis-auroratech.pdf (application/pdf)]

— Rishi Malhotra
Inference Optimization Lead, Redwood Inference

From: jasmine_liu@redwood.com

Subject: Re: RFI: Dedicated reservation sizing for AuroraTech inference — proposed commit and next steps

Alex / Procurement team — thanks for the sample and patience. Attached is a short reservation plan (spreadsheet) that reflects the internal fit. Executive summary below: 

- Proposed committed reservation (per primary region):
  • 5x H100‑profile nodes (targeted at long summarization and heavy generation)
  • 18x L4‑profile nodes (small‑chat, reranks, low‑latency ops)
  • 25% burst buffer (elastic shared pool) that can auto-burst to secondary region or hosted spare with policy-based throttling.

- Expected P95 at steady state (with KV cache, batching, and model quantization):
  • Chat (avg 80 tokens): 110–150 ms
  • Summarization (avg 900 tokens): 700–1,000 ms

- Notes on assumptions and options:
  • If AuroraTech is open to 4‑bit quantized variants for chat models on L4s, we can reduce L4 counts by ~20% while maintaining latency SLOs.
  • If synchronous latency is more important than cost, increase H100s by 1–2 nodes and reduce batching window to favor lower tail latency.
  • Cross‑region failover: suggest active/passive primary with automated fallback; cold standby adds ~30–45s to warm up large model caches unless prewarmed.

Next steps: please review the attached spreadsheet and tell us which option you prefer (cost‑optimized / latency‑optimized / hybrid). Once you pick, we will produce a formal SOW and committed pricing with SLA language.
